literal: What is called truthfulness, if you ask, is the speaking of words free from even the slightest harm to anyone.
translation: If one asks what truthfulness is, it is the speaking of words that are free from even the slightest harm to any living being.
modern: வாய்மை என்று சொல்லப்படுவது எது என்றால், அது எவ்விதத்திலும் யாருக்கும் தீமை இல்லாத சொற்களைப் பேசுவதாகும்.
explanation: In this couplet, the nature of truthfulness is defined not by literal accuracy, but by its impact. The author explains that true speech is that which is completely free from causing harm to any being. The phrase 'yātoṉṟum tīmai ilāta' emphasizes that even the smallest amount of harm must be absent. Therefore, the moral value of speech is determined by its benevolence and its capacity to prevent harm.
